reason: The heart needs pumping walls, so fitting heart muscle into the chambers seems like a useful place to start.
expectation: I expect the muscle to form the chamber walls, though the heart will still need valves and a rhythm.

alternatives.reason: Connecting vessels also advances a goal, but I want to build the pump first.

effect: The muscle now forms contracting chamber walls, so the pump still needs direction control.
reaction: The thickening outlines make the muscle's role clear.
reason: Add the valves to control blood flow through the chambers.
expectation: I expect the valves to fit into the chambers and help prevent reverse flow; the rhythm will still need attention.

alternatives.reason: The vessel network also serves a goal, but I want to finish assembling the pump first.

effect: The valves now give the chambers one-way flow; the pump still needs a rhythm.
reaction: The forward and reverse arrows make the valves' purpose clear.
reason: Add the pacemaker cells to complete the pump's rhythm.
expectation: I expect the cells to provide an electrical rhythm for the heart muscle.

alternatives.reason: The vessel network also advances a goal, but I want to finish the pump first.

effect: The heart now beats with its own electrical rhythm, completing the pump goal. The exchange route still needs assembling.
reaction: The distinction between starting the beat and nerves adjusting it is interesting.
reason: Connect the vessels and capillaries to build the exchange route and return path.
expectation: I expect a connected vessel network with capillaries between the outgoing arteries and returning veins.

alternatives.reason: Oxygen-carrying cells are also needed, but the vessel network directly addresses the remaining goal.

effect: The arteries, capillaries and veins now form a connected route beside tissue cells. The exchange-route goal has not yet been reported complete.
reaction: The arrows make the outward and return paths easy to follow.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and hemoglobin should help the red cells carry oxygen.
expectation: I expect oxygen-carrying red cells to form from the envelopes and hemoglobin.

effect: Red blood cells can carry oxygen and make ATP from sugar without mitochondria or a nucleus. They still need to be combined with plasma.
reaction: Their ability to make ATP without mitochondria is interesting.
reason: Combine the cells with plasma; it is the only offered combination and should form blood for the vessel route.
expectation: I expect blood containing red cells suspended in plasma.

effect: The red cells are now suspended in plasma as oxygen-carrying blood, ready for the vessel circuit.
reaction: The inset makes clear that blood includes other components too.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and adding blood to the circuit should advance the exchange-route goal.
expectation: I expect blood to fill the connected vessels and reach the capillaries beside tissue cells.

effect: Blood now fills the vessel circuit, and the exchange-route goal is complete. The remaining goal is to circulate it.
reaction: The small dots crossing while red cells stay inside make exchange clearer, though the dots are not identified.
reason: Connect the beating heart to the blood-filled circuit to put blood into circulation; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the heart to pump blood through the vessels and back to the heart.

effect: The heart and blood-filled vessels now form a closed circulation serving multiple tissues, completing the chapter.
reaction: Seeing the route return to the heart brings the separate constructions together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the heart to the blood-filled circuit was most worthwhile because it brought the pump, blood and vessel route together into a working system.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining plasma with red blood cells felt fairly predictable, especially as it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that red blood cells make ATP from sugar despite having no mitochondria, and that the heart starts its own beat while nerves can adjust it.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the small dots crossing the capillary wall were not identified, leaving the exchange a little unclear.

continue.text: I would continue: assembling circulation connected cellular needs to a body system, and the differences between heart and red blood cells made me curious about what comes next.
